_comment: Verification-probe marker registry. scripts/pack-portable.ps1 reads this file and
refuses to package a release whose frontend entry point (src/main.tsx) or built
bundle (dist/assets/*.js) contains ANY marker listed below, because a shipped app
must never be a temporarily-swapped-in acceptance probe.
WHY A REGISTRY RATHER THAN A HARD-CODED LIST IN THE PACKAGER: the old guard grepped
'SKIN RESULT', 'ACCEPTANCE RESULT', 'RESULT PASS', 'data-case='. Three of those match
nothing in this tree, and 'RESULT PASS' can never match because MainAcceptance.tsx
builds its verdict with a TEMPLATE literal (`RESULT ${cond ? "PASS" : "FAIL"}`) — the
contiguous string does not exist in the source or the bundle. Measured hits: 0. The
guard was decorative. The markers now live next to the probe that emits them, so the
probe owner updates them, not whoever remembers the packager's regex.
THE REGISTRY IS NOT SELF-ATTESTING. pack-portable.ps1 cross-checks it against every
probe under scripts/verify/*.tsx:
* each probe must declare  const DEVHUB_PROBE_MARKER = "<literal>";
* that literal must appear in `markers` below  (unregistered probe = hard stop),
* a registered marker that no probe emits as a quoted literal is reported as dead,
* a missing file, a missing `markers` array, an empty list or a blank entry are all
hard stops — the guard never degrades into 'nothing to check, therefore green'.
Exercise the whole guard without a release build:
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/pack-portable.ps1 -CheckProbeOnly
MARKER RULES (so a release never trips on them by accident):
* a plain STRING LITERAL present verbatim in the probe source, never a comment
(comments are stripped by the bundler, so a comment-only marker protects
src/main.tsx but NOT dist/assets/*.js),
* never a template-interpolated fragment (same reason 'RESULT PASS' failed),
* distinctive enough that product code will never contain it.
Add a probe -> add its marker here. If the list is empty or this file is missing,
the packager throws rather than shipping an unverified bundle.
